name: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention
problem: Existing sparse-attention methods either lack the arithmetic intensity to run fast on real hardware (they degrade memory-bound kernels into launch-bound ones) or cannot be trained end-to-end for pretraining - so they are post-hoc accelerators that require already-trained dense checkpoints.
mechanism: Natively trainable sparse attention with three components: (1) a hardware-aligned TILE-SPARSE attention pattern sized to the SRAM capacity of the target GPU so selected tiles actually fit; (2) an ARITHMETIC-INTENSITY-BALANCED algorithm design with implementation optimisations for modern hardware; (3) auxiliary loss terms that keep the compressed/selected representation faithful, enabling end-to-end pretraining rather than post-hoc pruning.
speedup_reported: PARTIAL - direction only, no multiple. The abstract states NSA achieves substantial speedups over FULL ATTENTION on 64k-length sequences across DECODING, forward propagation and backward propagation, and that a model pretrained with NSA maintains or exceeds Full-Attention models on general benchmarks, long-context tasks and instruction reasoning. No multiplier, no baseline settings, no hardware named in the abstract. What IS precise and useful is the claim's shape: speedups on all three phases (decode, fwd, bwd), not just prefill.
